title: Fall of the Soviet Union & End of Cold War
summary: The dissolution of the Soviet Union (USSR) into 15 independent nations, marking the end of the Cold War era.
facts: Mikhail Gorbachev resigned as President of the USSR on December 25, 1991.
The Soviet hammer and sickle flag over the Kremlin was lowered and replaced with the Russian tricolor.
Reshaped global geopolitical alliances and trade markets.

title: Reunification of Germany
summary: The official political reunification of East Germany (GDR) and West Germany (FRG) following the fall of the Berlin Wall in November 1989.
facts: The Two Plus Four Agreement signed in Moscow paved the way for unity.
Official Unity Day (Tag der Deutschen Einheit) celebrated on October 3, 1990.
Berlin was reinstated as the capital of reunified Germany.

title: Hubble Space Telescope Launch & Repair
summary: The deployment of the Hubble Space Telescope into low Earth orbit, followed by a famous 1993 Space Shuttle servicing mission to fix spherical aberration in its primary mirror.
facts: Deployed by Space Shuttle Discovery mission STS-31 in April 1990.
Initial images were blurry due to a 2.2-micron flaw in mirror curvature.
STS-61 servicing mission in December 1993 installed COSTAR optics, producing breathtaking deep space imagery.

title: Y2K Bug Preparation & Global Panic
manufacturer: Global IT Industry / Financial & Government Institutions
summary: Massive worldwide software remediation effort to correct two-digit year code representations in legacy software before the rollover to year 2000.
facts: Cost an estimated $300 billion to $600 billion globally in software updates and system testing.
Fears included potential power grid failures, bank lockouts, and transportation disruptions.
Systematic remediation prevented widespread catastrophic failures on January 1, 2000.

title: Dolly the Sheep Cloning
summary: The first mammal successfully cloned from an adult somatic cell using somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT).
facts: Born on July 5, 1996, at the Roslin Institute in Scotland, led by Ian Wilmut and Keith Campbell.
Named after country singer Dolly Parton.
Sparked worldwide ethical debates regarding genetic engineering and human cloning.
